correctness.rationale: For \(0<jf<1\) the two eigenvalues are exactly \(1\) and \(-jf\). Cayley–Hamilton proves the power formula for every positive integer \(m,n\); trace and determinant prove the exact factorization. Positivity of \(A^mB^n\) and \(|\det(A^mB^n)|<1\) prove the companion eigenvalue is below one and hence the sign classifies the Perron root. The averaged and long-spell conclusions follow by separate determinant and spectral-projector computations. Exact rational finite checking reproduced 10,816 block cases and positive averages, with no claim that finite checks establish unbounded cases.

value.rationale: Individually neutral environments leave the sign of population change under seasonal alternation undetermined. The theorem provides a complete nontrivial two-stage classification tied to an interpretable survival–fecundity tradeoff, and shows its sign is robust to arbitrarily unequal, positive spell durations. It also identifies what temporal averaging gets qualitatively correct in this boundary case. The exact sharp dichotomy is mathematically and ecologically motivated and is not asserted to predict empirical persistence outside the given deterministic model.
